The pair marched up the stairs, Hofner leading and Rovshana limping at his heel, eyes respectfully downcast. Outside, gunfire began to sound- the riot must have intensified. Hofner began to walk faster.

The pair reached the top of the staircase and swung open the exit to the helipad. There was nothing there.

"Wait a damn minute, where"s my heli-" The butt of a rifle swung into the back of Hofner"s skull, knocking him to the ground. As he lay on the ground, head pounding in agony, he heard a voice begin to speak in [RUS.GetAdjective].

"Thank you, Rovshana. Your payment is on the way."

options.name: "Scarlet base, this is Echo Five. I have the package."

title: Rapprochement
desc:
The sun was shining in Prince Sturzda"s garden. The geriatric nobleman, once a bloodsoaked servant of the long gone Iron Guard, spent most days in the overgrown plot now. There was little reason to leave. The Romanian Foreign Ministry, the bureaucracy he"d spent most of his life submerged within, was finally purified. Its halls were stuffed with Legionaries, as they should have been twenty years ago. The Jews and the weak men that permitted their infiltration were dead. The administration churned along, cutting away the vines of uncertainty and  marking the path for the Romano-Dacian race. Sturzda didn"t believe he'd live to see Romania"s complete triumph; he was nearing his ninetieth birthday, and he"d soon be home with his shepherd. Or was he nearing his ninety-first? It was hard to remember.

Mihai Botezatu, the Prince"s assistant, pushed his wheelchair down an uneven path. A beautiful patch of daffodils were blooming just out of the Prince"s sight. He couldn"t recall if they were the soft yellow Antonia had loved, or the pure, blanched white he"d come to admire in his later years.

"Beautiful day out, isn"t it?" Mihai said.

"It is," the Prince said. "The most beautiful I"ve seen in seven years. Ah, I remember the summer of "65. Of course, back then the country was still infested..."

Sturzda"s voice trailed off as he remembered the dark times. When it seemed that foolish King had separated Romania from her destiny forever, when their natural allies in Germany seemed to turn their backs on his motherland. The dark days when only Sturzda"s silver tongue and his faith had kept the movement alive.

"Well, we don"t need to worry about that anymore, sir," Mihai said. "You saved us all."

Sturzda smiled. Yes, he supposed he had.

"By the way," Mihai said, "a missive just arrived from the head office. There"s a situation in Baku. Of course, you"ve trained them so well, the junior ministers can handle it themselves."

Sturzda nodded. "Yes, I agree. I"m quite confident in their abilities. Tell them to use the usual channels."

Mihai pressed a pen and paper into the Prince"s hands. The paper had clearly been taken from a longer briefing, and contained a line for the Prince"s signature, acknowledging and accepting the briefing"s recommendations.

options.name: He smiled, signed the paper, and returned to his garden.

title: Reproached
desc:
Kurt Fuchs stood in his superior"s office, a friendly smile on his face. "Heil Hitler!" he shouted.

"Heil [Root.GetLeader]," Ministerialdirigent Schulze said. He was an older man, bald, with circular black glasses. Yet he was not the flabby sort of geriatric; his mind was like the end of a bayonet, quick and deadly sharp. "Fuchs, your salute is inappropriate. I advise you to change it."

Kurt simply broadened his smile. "Why, Herr Ministerialdirigent? I am simply stating my commitment to our race"s glorious past. Isn"t that precisely what National Socialism was created to defend?"

Schulze shook his head in frustration. "This isn"t why I brought you here, Fuchs. I heard from Till that you took a three day vacation during the Norwegian crisis."

Kurt nodded. "Well, you heard correctly. I made an executive decision to enjoy a brief sabbatical to the Black Forest with my wife."

"In the middle of a crucial diplomatic negotiation, you went on a weekend trip?"

"Yes, and I still accomplished all of our goals," Fuchs said. "The Norwegians joined the war, just as we planned. I"m not one for self-aggrandizement, but I have to say I"m quite proud of how things played out." He flashed a porcelain smile. His boss did not return the favor.

"Fuchs, I want to be quite clear," he said, leaning over his desk. Suddenly, Fuchs realized how the older man"s muscles bulged beneath his starched shirt. "Your actions during the Norwegian negotiations were completely unacceptable. I hold my subordinates to the highest standards. You will not desert your post while you lead the Romanian negotiations."

Fuchs furrowed his brow. "The Romanian negotiations, sir? I was told König would take charge of that issue."

"Not anymore," Schulze said. "Your success with the Norwegian issue has bought you friends in high places. But, he said, stabbing his index finger at Fuch"s chest, "point one toe out of line, and I"ll go straight to the Reichsminister."

title: Refocus
desc:
"Alright, Till," Kurt Fuchs said, "lay out the issue for me."

Till nodded. "Yes sir. As with the Norwegian crisis, our overall goal is to draw the Romanians into the war. With the situation deteriorating in Kausasia, their armed forces could be the difference between Total Victory and..." His voice trailed off. He licked his lips, and squeaked out the final phrase. "... defeat."

Fuchs snorted in disbelief. "Terrible situation, that we would have to rely on the armies of subhumans. I"m sure the Jews are responsible."

"Yes sir."

"Nevertheless, we must overcome their dreadful machinations. Tell me about this Costel Hoffmann."

"He"s a Romanian businessman, originally from the city of Chisinau."

"Moldovan, then? Perhaps some anti-Soviet sympathies."

"Indeed, Herr Fuchs. Hoffmann is a longtime member of the NSDAP. We hired him to help manage oil production in Baku, part to build relationships with their government, and part to avoid remnants of Josais" government. The [RUS.GetAdjective]s apparently sent a special forces unit to capture him during the fall of Baku."

"Why?” Fuchs asked. "Are they holding him for ransom?"

"No sir. They want to put him on trial. The Romanians need our diplomatic muscle to secure his release."

"Of course," Fuchs said, flashing his movie-star smile. "We"re always happy to assist our allies. Please send a missive to the [RUS.GetAdjective] foreign ministry, demanding his return."

options.name: "I"ll help you make the wording less... reasonable."

title: Smell the Gunpowder
desc:
Vladan Gurin's office was ice cold, as always. Not the mild chill of a skating rink or a shimmering Christmas morning blanketed in white. No, it was the frigid pain of numb fingers, the glacial agony of marching through knife-like snow without shoes. It was the cold of lost limbs, of frost in your eyebrows and burning ears. And somehow, the bastard liked it.

Sometimes Anya wondered if he was even human. “I haven't received any information about the crisis,” she said. She sat across from Gurin, cradling the dregs of ground-filled coffee.

Gurin frowned. "Yes, I was told you attempted to break protocol. Remember that our enemies are always listening." He removed a manilla folder from his coat pocket and threw it onto the desk. "Are you aware of Operation: Eiffel?"

She shook her head no. "Good," Gurin said. "Operation: Eiffel was a special forces initiative to capture and detain one Costel Hoffmann. He's a Romanian citizen and a long-time ambassador to Germany. The Reich hired him to manage the most productive oil field in Baku."

Anya put her closed fist to her mouth, deep in thought. "The special forces wouldn't go to this level of effort just to grab a Nazi. There's something you aren't telling me."

Gurin smiled like a wolf enjoying the hunt. "Well done, Ms. Kalashnik. We have significant evidence tying Hoffmann to both the German and Romanian intelligence agencies."

"I have to imagine the Romanians want him back, then."

"The Germans sent us a missive. It arrived a few hours ago." Gurin removed a copy from his desk and began to read. "To the criminal barbarians who claim to be the remnants of the [RUS.GetAdjective] government: you have kidnapped a citizen of our ally, [ROM.GetNameDef]. Your illegal and primitive methods do not go unnoticed. Release Costel Hoffmann or face the Reich's wrath." He chuckled. "More useful as toilet paper."

"We aren't going to release him."

"No. The special forces are going to interrogate him. Our job is to draft a reply to the Germans. Go get your typewriter. And tell me." he said, flashing a predator's smile, "What do you think about "To the government of the dying Reich?"

title: Something is Afoot
desc:
Prince Sturzda had dozed off in lapping waves of warm sunlight when he felt a twinge of pain in his back. He winced as electric agony shot up and down his spine, only to disappear a heartbeat later.

Mihai Botezatu grabbed Sturzda by the arm. "Are you okay? Do you need me to call a doctor?"

Sturzda wrenched his arm away. "I'm fine. Just part of being old." He shook his head. The nobleman felt as though there were cobwebs behind his eyes. "What were we talking about?"

"Daffodils, sir."

"Ah, yes!" Prince Sturzda smiled despite himself. "You know, Antonia used to love daffodils. I brought them to her every chance I could. I once gathered up a great bundle and hid them under the sheets of our bed. Imagine her surprise!"

"I can only imagine, sir."

"That reminds me, you haven't gotten married yet, have you?" Sturzda wagged his finger at Mihai. "I'll have to talk to my contacts in the Ministry. I'm sure one of them has a good, Christian niece."

"My duty to the nation comes before any other calling," Mihai said. "Speaking of which, I have another paper for you to sign. The Foreign Office needs permission to take some measures in regards to Baku."

Sturzda frowned. "Measures? You're sure there's nothing I need to help with?"

"Not to my knowledge. It's really a minor situation, nothing they can't handle."

"Nonetheless, maybe I need to be briefed on it."

"Prince Sturzda, I promise, there's nothing wrong," Mihai said. "Just a minor diplomatic kerfuffle. You've built up the Ministry over a lifetime, filled it with good men loyal to Romania. Now you have to trust them to build on your legacy."

"But-"

Mihai cut the Prince off. "Let's go look at the daffodils. I think there's a patch blooming at the end of the path."

A smile crossed Sturzda's wrinkled face. "I'd like that. Antonia loved daffodils. Did you know, I once gathered up a whole bundle and hid them in our bed? She kept them for weeks after."

"No, I haven't heard that story before." Mihai turned Sturzda's wheelchair away from the midday Sun, and towards the winding path. "Before we go, you said you'd sign these papers."

options.name: "I must have forgotten. Did you bring a pen?"

title: The Crisis Escalates
desc:
Kurt Fuchs nearly spat out his tomato soup when he heard the news. "They did WHAT?"

"The Romanians are grabbing [RUS.GetAdjective] citizens off the streets," Till said. "They're hostages. The Romanians say they'll expatriate them only once they get Hoffmann back."

"Jesus, this is too easy! Bastards are practically doing my job for me." Kurt waved to a nearby waiter. "Hey, we're celebrating. Send out a bottle of your best Spätburgunder."

Till leaned back in his seat, a dour look on his face. He picked at his salad aimlessly.

"Is something wrong?"

He sighed. "Listen, boss. We went to all this trouble to pin the Norwegian crisis on the [RUS.GetAdjective]s. Made a whole fake committee so we could keep the world's opinion on our side. And now you're going to let these Nazi puppets throw all that work away? If we don't condemn the kidnappings, the world is going to think we're allied to monsters."

Just as Kurt was about to reply, the waiter tapped him on the shoulder. "Sir, your wine." He bowed, placed the bottle on the table with a flourish, and left. And as he marched away from the table, he slid two pieces of paper into Kurt's lap. One, a handwritten note. It read, in scrawling script, "Meet me in the kitchen."

The second, a picture of Kurt and his wife in the Black Forest.

They'd been watching him for a long time.

options.name: "Jesus. Sorry Till, I have to go."

title: Hostage Situation
desc:
Mister Fuchs. Thank you for joining me," the tuxedo-clad man said. Kurt shivered in the restaurant's frigid meat locker, but the nameless person who'd impersonated his waiter hardly batted an eye. Precut steaks lay on metal racks on every side, and pork shoulders hung from hooks. The air stank of blood and rot.

"Don't thank me," Kurt said. "You're about two seconds away from a call to the Orpo. You want to tell me why you have a picture of my wife and I, or do you want to tell them?"

The nameless man smiled. "We have more than that." He dug into his tuxedo pocket, and removed two pictures. "You live at Kantstraße 41, 10625 Germania. You leave for work promptly between 07:30 and 07:38 every day. Your wife frequents the grocery store on Schlüterstraße 59, and makes your dinner fresh every day. She is devoted, and loyal." He revealed the first of the two Polaroids- a snapshot of subminister Fuch's wife, Klara, washing dishes at an open window. Wait, there was something wrong...

Klara hadn't had that haircut in three years.

"Jesus Christ," Fuchs whispered. "How long have you been watching me?"

"Long enough to find this," the imposter said. He revealed the second photo- a grainy snapshot taken through a hotel window. And Fuchs was in bed...

Kurt's stomach dropped ten thousand feet."It was a mistake," the minister said. "Just one bad decision."

"I don't know if your wife will see it that way, Mister Fuchs."

"Why are you doing this?"

The nameless man smiled. "We have a relationship with Mister Costel Hoffman. He has information about the [RUS.GetAdjective] situation necessary to bring the war to a successful conclusion. You have been instructed to permit his imprisonment, or death, in order to bring the Romanians into the war. In return for the destruction of these photos, you will deescalate the situation, and ensure his successful extraction."

Fuchs stammered, unable to find a response to his assailant."T-this is blackmail. I'll have the Abwehr hunt you idiots down, I swear!" His mouth suddenly felt as though it was full of sand, and his head pounded.

The impersonator leaned in to whisper in Fuch's ear. "We are the Abwehr. And we can do worse than this.

title: Everybody Just Stay Calm
desc:
Vladen Gurin's knuckles flared white as he gripped the plastic receiver. He hung up, and looked at Anya with a grim expression on his face. Was he... angry?

"I have unfortunate news," Gurin said. "The Romanians have taken a number of ethnic [RUS.GetAdjective]s hostage throughout their tin-pot dictatorship. Apparently, they will only guarantee their safety if Costel Hoffmann is released in the next three days."

"We can't do that."

"I agree that it's an undesirable outcome. Neither is a massacre." Gurin stood from his desk, and began to pace about the room. "What's more interesting is that the Germans have condemned the kidnappings. Their Foreign Ministry is putting pressure on the Romanians to release the hostages unharmed." He smiled like a creature from another world imitating a human being. "Perhaps they want to prevent another Bucharest."

Anya smiled, genuinely, even as she shivered like a pilot crashed in the Himalayas. "That could be our opening to keep the Romanians out of the war! Do you think the Germans are genuine?"

"Impossible to say. The underling I spoke to seemed disgusted enough, but he may have more moral fiber than the Ministry's leadership. If they condemn this criminal act, it is only because they see an advantage."

"They want Hoffmann's intelligence, and to maintain their international image," Anya said. "And we keep the Romanians off of the Southern front."

Gurin nodded. "Ethical issues often come down to issues of mathematics." Anya's superior ended his pacing, and sat down in front of her. "If we don't release Hoffmann, the evidence suggests the Romanians will kill these people. Several hundred of them, in fact. And if they enter the war, they will kill many of our soldiers on the Southern front. Their army is numerous, and disciplined. But."

He held up a finger. "But if we release Hoffmann, our intelligence networks will be compromised. Informants, and their families, will be killed. Officers will be assassinated. Supply depots will be destroyed. Our communications will be intercepted, and thousands will be killed across the frontline."

Anya couldn't bring herself to look him in the eye. She stared at the carpeted floor as she spoke. "You taught me to make sacrifices to achieve a better position."

"I did. The question is, which is the right sacrifice?"

options.name: "We can't release Hoffmann. If his intelligence gets out, thousands will be killed."

title: No Negotiations with Terrorists
desc:
Vladen Gurin's knuckles flared white as he gripped the plastic receiver. He hung up, and looked at Anya with a grim expression on his face. Was he... angry?

"I have unfortunate news," Gurin said. "The Romanians have taken a number of ethnic [RUS.GetAdjective]s hostage throughout their tin-pot dictatorship. Apparently, they will only guarantee their safety if Hoffmann is released in the next three days."

"We can't do that."

"I agree that it's an undesirable outcome. Neither is a massacre." Gurin stood from his desk, and began to pace about the room. "They've already killed twenty five of the hostages. Mostly women and children. The Guard hung them on meat hooks and tortured them to death." Anya's superior trembled. His face began to turn red, and he clenched and unclenched his fists.

Anya felt tears begin to form in the corners of her eyes. She swallowed a sob. "We can't let them do this."

Gurin took a deep breath. He took a deep breath, then another, then another. His face was a shade less red when he spoke again. "We can't let them set a precedent of terror, either. If the world sees that taking [RUS.GetAdjective] citizens hostage will result in leverage over our government, we'll see our people grabbed off the street everywhere. Colombia. Indonesia. South Africa. Anywhere there's terror, our people will be in danger."

Anya shifted in her seat. "What are you saying?"

"We'll talk to the President. War with Romania seems to be inevitable."

options.name: For hate's sake, they spit their last breath at us.

title: Our Asset Released
desc:
Excellent news out of Baku. Our intelligence asset there has been pried from [RUS.GetAdjective] hands. Of course, we owe this excellent outcome to our up and coming star, Mihai Botezatu. It was only through his clever strategy  and quick thinking that we were able to achieve this diplomatic success. We have everything we wanted, and we will not be drawn into the Second West [RUS.GetAdjective] War.

Mister Botezatu must be immediately treated as a candidate for promotion, and should be nominated for any awards deemed appropriate by the central government. He has my full confidence in his ability to carry out our national and racial duties, and I believe his career will be a boon to [ROM.GetNameDef].

Signed,

Prince Sturzda

options.name: Guess all those afternoons sweet talking the Prince paid off.

title: Our Asset is Imprisoned
desc:
Unacceptable news out of [RUSGetUniqueNamePlain]. Our intelligence asset there has been imprisoned at [RUS.GetAdjective] hands. A Romanian citizen, a close friend of the party and a National Patriot, has been imprisoned for the sake of his loyalty and his unwavering resolve in the face of Judeo-Bolshevik aggression. There is only one reasonable response to this: an immediate declaration of total war against the [RUS.GetAdjective] government.

Alongside our allies, the German Reich, we intend to force the barbarians over the Urals and into the Siberian wastes. Once again, the pure races will stand side by side in a struggle for western civilization and against barbarity. Our nation will be renewed by the tides of struggle, and our boys will grow into men under the caring dotage of machine gun fire. This is a time of heroes, and Romania is nothing if not a heroic nation.

title: Stuck in Ukraine
desc:
The Lieutenant slumped in the commander's seat, sweat voyaging down his wrinkled forehead. He tried to rest his eyes, but it was no use. God, he felt like he was being cooked alive!

The radio roared to life. "Petrov, take a squadron of tanks to the field south of the town. Reports indicate several German units of varying quality and firepower withdrawing from the village." He sighed, and shifted his beast into gear.

The Russian tanks slipped around the bend of a forest outline and materialized on the flank of a German armored column. The ragged flock was formed of a mixture of panzers, military trucks, and foot infantry; spots of rust and flat tires accentuated their slovenly march. "Guess we'll put the bastards out of their misery," Petrov said. He spoke into his radio. "All units, open fire." Petrov's cannon ignited, striking the leading panzer straight in its side. Smoke began to billow from the panzer's cockpit as the Russian reapers scythed away a bloody harvest. The commander of the burning tank scrabbled out of his dying vehicle, only to be sawed in half by a burst of machine gun fire. Within a minute all that remained on the road was a heap of burning metal, and fifty seven mutilated soldiers.

title: Old Tricks
desc:
Two men were within the room, waiting for the call to come through. One was no more than a simple radio officer, one who'd served with the Wehrmacht since the end of the civil war. The other, an intelligence officer, did nothing but breathe and observe the same air that sat around the worn-out radio in silence. The silence that persisted felt like poison to the radio operator, as he prepared to respond to the most important call of his lifetime.

The radio sprang to life. It didn't take long for the radioman to find the right tone. "How many? 23 Hungarians? Officer, did you preserve the bodies or catch documentation? I see. In that case, repeat everything you can tell us about the victims."

The call went on for several more minutes. The radio officer played his part like the most brilliant Shakespearan, deftly recalling every detail of the script and forcing his faceless companion down every needed avenue. When the curtains fell, the intelligence officer turned the radio operator away from the battered transponder, and took down every detail of the emergency message, just as they'd practiced. Moments later, the Abwehr agent left the room to report the great tragedy that had unfolded at the hands of the Russian invaders.

options.name: The Hungarian Consulate received him five minutes later.

title: Germany Calls...
desc:
"We've got to make those fuckers pay, starting with helping our German allies," a Hungarian politician said. The German ambassador tapped his feet to the music filling his ears. "The Germans have demonstrated great respect and support for our regime. Only by tying our will to theirs can we ensure our joint success." A dozen Hungarians sat around the table with placards indicating each position they held, all being members of the 'Commission of Hungarian Damages in the German Reich.'

"As such we must examine the full damage by the Russian invaders, both material and human. I suggest demands that will grant our observers the ability to cross the front lines and question the related troops, and in addition financial repayments for the dead, whose bodies were seemingly destroyed by the Russian horde."

A dozen Hungarian eyes wandered, before settling on the head of the committee, hoping he'd provide a sense of approval.The balding man, sensing the weight of the room shifting, finally opened his mouth. "This is good. I will also officially call upon the Hungarian armed forces to be ready to force the Slavs to listen, should they be uncooperative."

The Germans smirk widened, and as the Hungarians started to collect their things, he walked out, ready report what he heard.

title: Dear Representatives of Hungary
desc:
...Please understand that we're treating this situation with the highest severity. While during wartime all manner of violent and horrible actions occur, we've actively attempted to mitigate such incidents from occurring.

As such we've started our own investigation into the incident. Several factors complicate the matter. For one, the nearest Russian units were still several kilometers away, and none of the troops we've investigated reported the sort of action you claim happened. While it has also been claimed that there should be remains in the area, our investigation suggests the only damage at the area during the time of death was several controlled fires seemingly started with gasoline and matches.

As such we have concerns regarding the validity of the accusations, especially since most information suggests the findings were not conducted by Hungarians, but rather German units that were in the area. With that being said, we've decided to...

title: The Rotten State of Hungary
desc:
There wasn't a street in Budapest where the announcement of the Russian rejection played well. The fascist regime's representatives turned out where they could. "A good war will give the new generation a real backbone. Today's youth are lazy; they don't understand what it took to build our nation's present greatness!" Whether the crowds gathered around the speakers truly believed, or simply stayed quiet, became quickly irrelevant. The press formed a whip, and drove the population into a frenzy.

Meanwhile, the same committee that sent the first demand prepared their next step. The soldiers loaded their rifles and laced their boots,  prepared to join the war and hopefully prevent the defeat of their German ally. The few voices that dared to suggest backing down would either be removed over several days or conveniently "convinced" to the necessity of demanding more from Russia or face war.

When the Committee found its senses and saw the natural necessity of decrying Russia, they elected to write another list of demands. The demands were more or less the same, with the only major difference being the severity of demands. Greater sums of reparations, more freedom in examining the Russian side of the frontlines.

title: Another Set of Demands
desc:
Fingers rolling over the fabric of his coat pocket, Pavlov waited for [RUS.GetLeader] to finish his military debriefing for the day. His eyes were already half closed- the overnight flight from Istanbul had beaten him like a mother with a dusty carpet. He fixated on the silky texture of his pocket, trying his damndest not to let the warm room get to him.

[RUS.GetLeader] clapped him on the shoulder, startling the diplomat awake. "Pavlov Alexeivich, was it? Tell me about our Hungarian problem. My eyes are much too tired to read another page of, well, anything."

Pavlov swallowed, and rubbed his eyes. "I have nothing good to report. The Hungarians are still posturing. The demands are more of the same- reparations, and Hungarian access to our communications, to prevent another 'incident'."

"And any information they gain will be funneled back to the Germans."

"Precisely. They're prepared to join the war unless their demands are accepted. And not just posturing. Anti-Russian propaganda has dramatically increased in the Hungarian state newspaper. They're mobilizing armored units and field hospitals. I predict they could enter the war within a month."

[RUS.GetLeader] laid back in their chair, and closed their eyes. Within five minutes, Pavlov had his answer.

title: Hungarian Rhapsody
desc:
The German ambassador took a deep breath of the fumes that filled the air, and looked upon his handiwork. The entirety of Liberty Square was filled with patriotic Hungarians chanting slogans like trained dogs. The energy of the square reminded him of the Nuremberg Rally in 1934, the days when Germany embarked on its journey to reclaim its glory. The same spirit of supremacy filled the air, but a key difference fouled the sweet scent of hatred.

The Hungarians were lying to themselves.

Even if Hungary took every ounce of strength and threw it decisively behind Germany, there was nothing for them to gain. Transylvania wasn't to be renegotiated. In the smoke-filled boardrooms, Germania planned to bind the states of Europe to their will. The fascist government in Hungary was always a glove to cover Germany's fist.

He felt no regret. In fact, he smiled. If he'd been a less serious person, he might have sung and danced, or downed a few bottles of liquor. His duty, and his joy, was to further Germany's interests.

options.name: Even if the price was Hungarian lives.

title: No Step Back
desc:
Pavlov readied himself to meet the leader of Russia once again. This time, he'd had eight hours and two cups of steaming coffee, no sugar. The early morning sun blazing through the windows made a much better sight than the same glass in total darkness. The door cracked open, and a nondescript soldier beckoned him inside.

[RUS.GetLeader] greeted Pavlov with a firm handshake. "I take it they haven't responded well to our delaying tactic?"

"No, and I must inform you we're out of time if we mean to give in to the Hungarian demands. We're down to our last few hours."

[RUS.GetLeader] wasn't quite used to dealing with Non-Russian diplomacy. There was a greater sense of lag and an increased number of intermediates. However, things remained much the same on one account, the casual suggestion of war as a solution. On that front, the world was very much similar. They sat and thought about the progress in the war and whether the front could handle an addition like the Hungarian army. Regardless of their decision, the war was going to be over soon, and only time would tell if they made the right call.

options.name: Cut all ties to the Hungarians, and get me the generals.

title: We Join the Second West Russian War!
desc: After the cowardly attack on our people, and the refusal of the Russian state to properly compensate us and aid in investigating this heinous attack on civillians, we have no choice but to join the German Reich to defend our nation and people.

options.name: Maybe we can perform well enough to get Transylvania back?

title: The End of Everything
desc: It is over. With our troops having recently entered Germany itself, it seems that the Führer has decided to use the nuclear option. Thousands of German nuclear missiles are already flying high in the sky, en-route to our population centers at supersonic speeds. There is nothing more to be done.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]End of the London Crisis
desc:
The citizens of the United Kingdom let out a sigh of relief. The Prime Minister of England has officially announced that the United Kingdom, after a tense diplomatic meeting with the [RUS.GetAdjective]s, will not be entering the War in Europe.

The world trembled at the shock of the London Airport Bombing, an event the Führer described as yet another “Slavic Judeo-Bolshevik scheme to destroy the Aryan people”. Many thought such a traumatic event would inspire the desire for revenge within the English people. However, it seems the spirit of British neutrality has not been broken after all. As the Second West [RUS.GetAdjective] war rages on, Britain will continue to sit on the sidelines, the ghosts of that night forever wandering the tarmac in search of closure.

options.name: England has chosen its path. Now it must follow it.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The United Kingdom Joins the West [RUS.GetAdjective] War
desc:
In a clear display of their commitment to the German alliance, the English government has formally declared war on [RUS.GetName]. Following the horrific London Airport Bombing, in which dozens of civilians were killed, [RUSGetUniqueNamePlain] attempted to maneuver blame for the deaths onto other parties. However, the English inquiry turned up evidence implicating the [RUS.GetAdjective] government. Attempts to resolve this dispute through diplomacy have failed, leaving the English no recourse but to attack those who murdered their countrymen.

While the rationale for the [RUS.GetAdjective]'s attack on England is unknown, the effects of this crisis are not. Well armed, well-supplied, and well trained English soldiers are bolstering the line in Eastern Europe, relieving fatigued German infantrymen and taking up defensive emplacements across the Vistula. London and Germania now seem closer than ever before.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Massacre in Romania
desc:
Terrible news out of Romania. For reasons unknown to the world, the Romanian State had imprisoned a number of [RUS.GetAdjective] citizens throughout the nation. Today, those individuals were killed en masse in circumstances described as "too horrible to discuss". Early estimates suggest over four hundred civilians were murdered

The [RUS.GetAdjective] government has condemned both the Romanians and the German Reich for permitting this mass killing. [RUS.GetAdjective] sources speaking off the record suggest the Germans encouraged the killings as retribution for the onset of the Second West [RUS.GetAdjective] War. The German Foreign Ministry has condemned the allegations, stating that "the Romanians acted of their own accord, without Reich direction or intervention." Both parties are sure of this: whatever the reason, this mass murder will only inflame tensions in Eastern Europe.

options.name: National Socialist barbarity on display once again.
If it did happen, then they deserved it.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Silence of the West
desc:
A wave of relief has hit the [RUS.GetAdjective] nation today. Thousands of ethnic [RUS.GetAdjective]s who had been held hostage by the Romanian government were let go after the Federation traded Costel Hoffmann, a Romanian asset in the Caucasus. Early estimates showed that an estimated four hundred and fifty [RUS.GetAdjective] would"ve been immediately lynched if not for the release of Hoffmann.

From this violent provocation the [RUS.GetAdjective] government vehemently condemned both the Romanian and German government for encouraging such barbaric acts. Though the German Foreign Ministry has condemned the allegations stating that "the Romanians acted of their own accord, without Reich direction or intervention.". Both parties are sure of this:Whatever the reason, such barbaric acts would only inflame tensions between the countries and lead to the escalation of the Second West [RUS.GetAdjective] War.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Baltic Crisis Averted
desc: After a period of intense diplomatic struggle, the Baltic Crisis has been defused by Russian diplomats. The destruction of the neutral merchant ship Njord by a Russian naval mine, already a terrible incident, threatened to spiral out of control as German diplomats worked behind the scenes to fan the flames of international outrage. Sources in both governments suggest the Norwegians were close to declaring war upon the Russian government. However, a last minute diplomatic breakthrough barely convinced the Norwegians to maintain the fragile peace. Scandinavia has avoided the whirlpool of modern warfare by a hair's breadth, for now. Only time will tell if peace can prevail in a continent defined by war.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Norway Joins The Second West Russian War
desc: In an unexpected turn of events, the Norwegian government has formally declared war on the [RUS.GetName]. The Norwegians initially declared their neutrality, intending only to bolster the Third Reich through arms shipments and preferential trade policies. However, the destruction of the Njord, a neutral merchant vessel crewed by Norwegian sailors, at the hands of a Russian naval mine pushed the Norwegian public and government towards war. Numerous opportunities for a peaceful resolution were bypassed by the Russian government. Now, a new front in the war for Europe has opened in Scandinavia. Will this change the tides of war in Germany's favor? Or will the Russians persevere through this extraordinary setback?

options.name: The forest of heathendom marches to war once more.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]London Airport Bombing
desc:
News emerged from London today regarding the explosion of a plane that had just landed from Germania, killing nearly everyone on board. Among the survivors was the German diplomat, Kurt Fuchs, who was en-route to a security conference with the British government regarding the ongoing Second West [RUS.GetAdjective] War. Currently the perpetrators are unknown, but already there are investigators trying to determine the cause of the explosion.

The German Reich has been quick to blame the [RUS.GetAdjective]s for the bombing, claiming that they attempted to disrupt their planned security conference with the British. The [RUS.GetAdjective]s on the other hand, have immediately denied their involvement with the incident.

options.name: Is this the end of British neutrality?

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Hungary Joins the Second West Russian War
desc:
In a repeat of the 1940s, the Hungarian army has mobilized to assist their German allies in Eastern Europe. Limited communication from the Hungarian regime states that the Republic intervened against the Russians "to protect civilian populations from Slavic barbarism". Speculation around the specific circumstance of the crisis remains at an all time high, with the German Bloc refusing to allow independent investigations into wartorn Eastern Europe. Russia has been no more open to international observers, and have stated any such efforts must come after the war officially ends.

While the Hungarian army isn't one of Europe's greatest, it may nonetheless become a factor in stemming the tide of the Russian advance, or even assist in pushing them out of Ostland and Ukraine.

options.name: Truth remains the first casualty in war.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Danubian Crisis Averted!
desc:
In an unexpected turn of events, Russia and Hungary have avoided coming to blows over what the International Press have come to call the "Massacre in Ukraine". A Russian tank brigade, seemingly without provocation, attacked and killed a number of Hungarian civilians while being escorted out of Ukraine by the Hungarian military. The Russian government has unreservedly apologized for the attack, and taken full responsibility in the eyes of the world.

Despite statements that "the truth will come out" from [RUS.GetLeader], Russia rests easy knowing it won't face another enemy in its war of liberation. The German government has made no official response to the news despite reportedly discovering the incident in question. Rumors from the  Reich suggest serious discontent with current circumstances.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Germany Surrenders!
desc: To many, the outbreak of the Second West Russian War was a futile effort by the new Russian Government, a campaign that was destined for failure from the moment the war had been declared yet the world watches on in shock as a spokesman speaking on behalf of the Führer has announced that in the interests of saving the Reich from Nuclear annihilation, the German government have decided to cede their eastern frontier to the rising [RUS.GetAdjective] State. The international and domestic embarassment of giving up their 'Lebensraum' has sent shockwaves across the globe. On the streets of Germany, protests have erupted across the nation as the Wehrmacht prepares to declare martial law. The consequences of the Treaty of Riga will have major repercussions on the German Reich for many years to come.

options.name: As one nation falls, another rises.
The Russians will pay one day.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Treaty of [400.GetName]
desc: As was expected by millions across the globe, the Wehrmacht has once more soundly beaten the armies of Russia. Diplomats and Generals from the Reich have gathered in the occupied city of [400.GetName] to discuss the terms of surrender with the [RUS.GetAdjective] government. After hours of debate with the [RUS.GetAdjective]s, the Germans and [RUS.GetAdjective]s have signed the Treaty of [400.GetName]. The terms saw the restoration of the borders of Moskowien and the ceding of Kazan & [850.GetName] to the Reickskommissariat. The effects of the treaty on [RUSGetUniqueNamePlain] have been devastating for the new [RUS.GetAdjective] government with some international spectators suspecting that [RUSGetUniqueNamePlain] would soon break apart into anarchy and begin a new age of Russian warlordism.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Liberation of Moscow
desc:
In recent weeks, no city has had more attention than the infamous city of Moscow. As the centre of German rule in Eastern Europe, and as the former capital of the Russian nation, Moscow was a prime objective for the Russian armies marching westward.

Momentum has shifted to the Russian side of the conflict, with the city falling under Russian hands. While the Germans are far from out of the war, their ability to reclaim Moscow remains slim. The city's fall has become a highly publicised event outside of the Reich, where many see Moscow's liberation as the beginning of the end of the Reich. Within The German bloc, censors are hard at work at preventing the spread of news regarding the significant defeat. Regardless, throughout the German sphere, voices of dissent are rapidly starting to rise, as doubt has begun to spread among the German public.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Federation Triumphs over the Einheitspakt
desc: In a shocking turn of events, the All-Russian Army has overcome the vast German armies. Overwhelmed by Russian air superiority and experienced soldiers, the Einheitspakt has formally surrendered to the Russian Federation in the hopes of avoiding all out nuclear war between the two countries. The Federation accepted, signing the Treaty of Riga, which saw the Einheitspakt hand over the lands of the former Soviet Union. Millions within the Reich's former imperial lands rejoiced as the winds of change finally arrived. Chaos has erupted in Germany as the people accuse the German government of weakness. Many factions from SS sympathizers to reformists have begun to battle it out on the streets while the Wehrmacht attempts to control the situation. Only time can tell what the complete repercussions of a Russian victory may have on both Europe and the globe.

options.name: As one superpower falls, another one rises.
A bright future awaits the Federation.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Federation Stands Triumphant
desc:
Cheers erupted across the Russian Federation when Alexander Pokryshkin announced the surrender of Germany. With staggering successes in the initial stages of the war, the Russian Federation was able to capitalize on confusion and discord among the Heer and push them back across the Russian plains, reclaiming Moscow for the Russian people. All of the death, oppression, and despair of the last few decades has been washed away by a wave of euphoria as Russia celebrates its victory over its western foe.

As rebuilding efforts begin across the regained Russian territory, Germany is in chaos as the once indomitable German military has found itself defeated by a people it considers inferior. There are already rumblings of renewed protests against the current regime, and more is sure to follow. The rest of the world, however, looks on with joy as light once more returns to the old world.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Vladivostok Returned to [RUS.GetNameDef]
desc:
After tense negotiations between the Japanese Empire and [RUS.GetNameDef], the two nations have met in Beijing to sign a treaty to resolve the territorial dispute.

The treaty saw the lands of Outer Manchuria and the city of Vladivostok reintegrated into [RUS.GetNameDef] in exchange for the safe passage of the 'Dongbei' peoples to Northern Manchuria and Korea.

Celebrations have occurred across [RUS.GetNameDef] over the nation's diplomatic victory over the Japanese. With Vladivostok returned to Russia, the world awaits [RUS.GetNameDef]'s next move as they turn their attention westwards, where Germany still holds Reichskommisariat Moskowien.

options.name: For the survival of the Empire.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Birobidzhan Returned to [RUS.GetNameDef]
desc:
After negotiations between the Japanese Empire and [RUS.GetNameDef], the two nations have met in Beijing to sign a treaty to resolve the territorial dispute.

The treaty saw the province of Birobidzhan reintegrated into the new Russian state in exchange for the end of the violence in the region and the return of the partisans back to Russia.

Although some in [RUS.GetNameDef] celebrated the peaceful return of Russian territory, many felt the Russian government didn't try hard enough to liberate their lands from Japanese occupation. With the issue of the Far East resolved for the time being, the world awaits [RUS.GetNameDef]'s next move as they turn their attention westwards, where Germany still holds Reichskommisariat Moskowien.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Bukharin Imprisoned!
desc:
Shocking news has emerged from the newly united Russian Federation as the former premier of the Soviet Union, Nikolai Bukharin, the man who famously led the Soviet Union into the jaws of the Nazi war machine, was found and arrested by members of the Sluzhba Bezopasnosti.

Once thought to have died following the fall of Moscow, the news of his capture and imprisonment were welcomed by most Russians living within the Federation, the populace happy that the man that had doomed them decades ago was finally getting the punishment he deserved. The Siloviks have applauded the President's actions.

President Vasily Shukshin, however, was unavailable for comment.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Russo-Japanese Negotiations Begin!
desc:
After weeks of partisan chaos and rising tension between [RUS.GetNameDef] and [JAP.GetNameDef], the Japanese have finally agreed to enter into negotiations with the [RUS.GetName] over the disputed territory of Outer Manchuria with hopes of reaching a peaceful with the nuclear armed power.

Diplomats from [RUS.GetNameDef] and the Co-Prosperity Sphere have met in the Chinese city of Beijing where the negotiations are to take place. International observers from the United States of America to the Italian Empire have also gathered in the city to observe the negotiations on behalf of their respective governments.

The discussions between the Japanese and the Russians may change the future of both Russia and Japan for many years to come.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Russia Regains Outer Manchuria
desc:
After tense negotiations between the Japanese Empire and [RUS.GetNameDef], the two nations have met in Beijing to sign a treaty that aims to resolve the territorial dispute.

The treaty saw the lands of Outer Manchuria reintegrated into [RUS.GetNameDef] and in exchange, Russia would assure the safe passage of the 'Dongbei' peoples to Northern Machuria and Korea.

Celebrations have occurred across [RUS.GetNameDef] over the nation's diplomatic victory over the Japanese. With the issue of the Far East now resolved, the world awaits [RUS.GetNameDef]'s next move as they turn their attention to the west where Germany still holds Reichskommisariat Moskowien.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Russia Declares War on Germany
desc: The world stands in shock as the recently reunified Russia has declared war on Germany with the public goal of the Russian government being to retake rightfully Russian lands from their German occupiers and make the Germans pay for their decades of humiliation. The German Reich has begun a process of mobilization against their old eastern foe, promising to both the German people and the world that the Russian nation would be defeated once more within only a few weeks. The world holds its breath as for the first time in history, two nuclear armed powers are going to be directly fighting against one another. With the fate of the world at stake, millions are praying that the conflict can be resolved soon without plunging the world into darkness.

title: [Get_newspaper_header][RUS.GetName] Intervenes in Iran
desc:
As the civil war continues to rage across Iran, [RUS.GetLeader] has announced the [RUS.GetName]'s formal intervention into the conflict.

Although its official aims are to restore order to the troubled region many international spectators agree that the true purpose of the [RUS.GetName]'s involvement is to expand its sphere of influence.

Although Russia has only recently reunified after decades of warlordism and already, [RUS.GetNameDef] has begun to make its moves on the world stage, upsetting the political status quo since the end of the Second World War.

The entry of the 'Fourth Power' into the Iranian Civil War has changed the balance of power in the conflict and could become influential in deciding the war's outcome.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Black Army Offensive Fails
desc:
Despite initial successes against the German forces in the Reichskommissariat Moskowien, the forces of the Russian anarchists have been pushed back by the Heer. The anarchists had hoped to free all of the former lands of Russia from the "tyranny of the state", but it appears that German control will continue to extend into Russian lands for the foreseeable future.

In a press statement, the German foreign minister has expressed satisfaction with the work of the German military, and promised that order and stability will return to Germany's eastern holdings. There is no official statement from the anarchist government, but sources within tell of an atmosphere of hopelessness. Starting only as a small band of rebels in central Siberia, their march for freedom appears to have ended.

options.name: The Slavic menace is brought to heel.
The black flag flies no more.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Stepanov's Gamble Fails
desc:
In a turn of events that has surprised few, the Germans have once again defeated a Russian invasion from their eastern border. The forces of the anarchists, led by Ivan Stepanov, were hoping for a final victory over the forces of the German Reich. The Heer and Luftwaffe have given them no such satisfaction, and now Stepanov's forces must turn home and deal with the domestic situation currently brewing. For the foreseeable future, Germany shall have no threat from the east.

The German foreign minister has stated that he is confident the administration will be able to put down the last of the resistance in the eastern territories. Ivan Stepanov, leader of the anarchist forces, has been silent for much of the campaign. Whether he will be able to hold the lands he now controls is unlikely, and it appears a new age of warlordism is soon to come to Russia.

options.name: Our power wanes, and so do our people.
The black warlord has been driven from our land!
The vanguard withers against the German eagle.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Second West Russian Disaster
desc:
The Red Army invaded the Reichskommissariat Moskowien once more hoping to smash the German war machine and liberate their lands from fascist rule, and once more they were pushed back by the forces of the Wehrmacht and Luftwaffe in a rain of bombs and bullets. Both sides suffered heavy losses as hundreds of thousands are left rotting in the plains of Russia. The liberation of the Russian lands has failed, and the Red Army poses no more threat to Germany's eastern empire.

The German foreign minister expressed satisfaction at the Wehrmacht once again crushing the Red Army. The Soviet foreign minister has issued their own statement that, even in its loss, the spirit of socialism will never leave the Russian nation and that one day, the Soviet Union would rise from the ashes once again. Most experts remain skeptical on whether this new Russian state will last the next few months.

options.name: Our vanguard of the revolution crumbles.
The Reds will never beat Aryan might.
The Red Army has failed once again.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Red Army Surrenders
desc:
For the first time in twenty years, the Red Army crossed into the Russian lands controlled by the German Reich in order to free their people from the iron grip of Nazi rule. Grand Marshal Tukhachevsky promised that his Red Army would utterly obliterate the Germans. And after months of brutal fighting which has left hundreds of thousands dead or injured, the Soviet forces have been pushed back once more. Germany's enemies now mourn the lost chance of destroying Reich power in the east, while Germany celebrates its final victory over Bolshevism.

The German government has promised that the administration will do its best to repair the damage done to the eastern territories, and that colonization efforts will resume by the end of the year. Sources in the Soviet government have expressed concern over the Marshal's health in recent days, and whether the government has the strength to hold its territory.

options.name: The Red Napoleon has lost his final battle.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Bolsheviks Surrender
desc:
All the hopes of the free world rested on the success of the Soviet army to crush the German forces. And after months of brutal fighting across the Russian plains, the Wehrmacht has once more declared victory against the forces of Bolshevism. With the destruction of the Soviet army, Suslov's government has been forced to the negotiating table. German rule in the east will continue for the foreseeable future, and all of the free world mourns the loss.

The Soviet foreign minister promised that the loss was not a permanent one, and that Soviet rule of the remaining Russian lands would continue, while the American Secretary of State declared that German influence will be fought in every corner of the globe, and that this is only a minor setback. The German foreign ministry simply expressed their gratitude to the heroes of the Wehrmacht.

options.name: The weakness of Bolshevism is revealed!
Marx's teachings have failed once more.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]March of Progress Ends
desc:
The armies of the Soviet Federation have been defeated by the forces of the Wehrmacht after brutal fighting all across the Russian plains. After initially pushing the Germans back, they were not able to keep their gains as they were steadily pushed out of the German colonial territory. A disaster for the free world, they had rested their hopes on the newly reformed Communist government despite some of its more eccentric qualities. It now seems that the futurist lens through which the Russians have been living for the last few years has shattered in failure.

The German people are elated at their victory, with celebrations throughout the streets of Germania. The free world mourns with Russia, and it's unclear what the Soviet's next move may be. Suffice to say, they will not be able to threaten Germany's colonial possessions for the foreseeable future.

options.name: The red star falls back to Earth.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Daughter of Socialism Surrenders
desc:
The forces of the Soviet Union, led by the energetic daughter of the previous Soviet leader, Bukharin, have been forced to the negotiating table by the Wehrmacht. After initial successes which left much of the free world hopeful that a wave of freedom was about to wash over German occupied Europe, the soldiers of the Reich were able to stem the tide and turn the red wave back, securing their hold over the Russian plains. There is little doubt that they will not see a threat from the east in the near future.

The Russian leader, Bukharina, has locked herself away with her closest advisors to discuss what comes next. Some unnamed sources already fear that cracks are beginning to show in the newly reformed Soviet Union. The Germans are elated at the reversal of fortunes on their eastern border, while the Americans have expressed their condolences to the Russian people.

options.name: The daughter falls same as the father.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Reds Surrender
desc:
The whole of the free world waited with bated breath for the collapse of German dominance in Europe. The Germans have proven that faith mistaken, however, as they reversed the initial gains by Soviet forces and forced them back across the border. Kaganovich's government, brutal and harsh in its directives, put all its hopes on a victory in the west. With this loss, there are some fears about what may follow for the newly reunified Russian state.

The German people celebrate their victory over Bolshevism, with renewed faith in their government and party as the celebrations almost match that which followed the first victory in the east. The Americans have expressed regret, but promise to continue the fight. The Soviet government has yet to make an official statement, and there are reports from within that Kaganovich is planning a purge against traitorous elements who stunted the war effort.

options.name: Someone is to blame for this...

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Soviet Disaster
desc:
When the Soviets crossed the border into the Reichskommissariat Moskowien, Nikita Khrushchev was confident that the Soviet forces would crush their German opponents "beneath the heel of Marxist progress". Now, the leader of the Soviet Union has little to say as the Germans, after suffering initial defeats at the hands of Soviet forces, have managed to push them back and once more secure their control over the Russian plains.

The hopefulness that had filled the streets of Soviet cities and towns before the invasion has disappeared, and an air of suspicion has replaced it as ministers and officials blame one another for their failure. As celebrations erupt across the German Reich, anxiety and fear now rules across the Soviet Union as the people wait for what the consequences of this loss may be.

options.name: Germania rises and the world weeps.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Soviet Forces Admit Defeat
desc:
To the disappointment of many all over the free world, the Soviet Union has once more been defeated by the Wehrmacht. Many had hoped that, with the reunification of Russia under the leadership of Yagoda, they would have the strength and fortitude to crush the German army. Yet, after months of brutal fighting which have left hundreds of thousands of widows grieving across Eurasia, the Soviets have been forced to admit defeat.

Celebrations are reported across Germany, but especially by Germans in the untouched colonial possessions which were under threat by the Soviet invasion. Officials within the Soviet government are blaming one another for the loss, but none more than the NKVD, who are calling for a new round of purges to eliminate what they see as "domestic dissidents" who held back the war effort. It seems the Russian bloodletting is not yet over.

options.name: You can't win a war with Gulags.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Presidium Announces Surrender to Germans
desc:
All eyes were turned on the Soviet Union during the last few months in the hope that the rejuvenated Communist state could finally roll back German dominance over Europe. Despite managing to push the Germans across much of the Russian plains, the forces of the Wehrmacht were able to mount a successful counter-attack which devastated the Soviet military. The Reich has once more secured its eastern holdings as the people of Germany celebrate their third victory over Bolshevism.

The American State Department has vowed that it will continue to fight fascist influence across the globe, and that this is only a minor setback. Back in the halls of the Soviet government, the mood is much more dire. Many question Bessonov's leadership, and many more fear for the continued stability of the Union following this disastrous defeat. One thing is certain: Russia will not threaten Germany again.

options.name: The Marxist dream dies with us.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Dream Dies
desc:
When the Soviet Union announced its invasion of Germany's eastern territories, the world held its breath. Now, they mourn with the people of Russia as the Soviet Union announces its surrender to German forces. Despite initial successes against the Wehrmacht, the German military managed to recoup much of its territory. The Soviet government has been forced to acknowledge the territorial gains of the Germans taken in World War 2, and the world weeps for the tragedy that shall follow for the people of the Russian plains.

Celebrations have erupted across the German Reich, with the German colonial settlements in the East the most ecstatic. Sablin, leader of the renewed Soviet Union, has been quiet following the loss. Sources within the government speak of a dejected leader, in stark contrast to his earlier demeanor. The last shred of hope has been sapped from the Russian people.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]German Forces Prevail
desc:
The Russian government has announced its surrender to German forces as the Russian military has been routed from the territories of the Reichskommissariat Moskowien. Svetlana Stalina, leader of the Russian government, announced the defeat over radio before returning to her offices to discuss with her advisors what comes next. Most international observers fear for the stability of a regime that staked so much of its existence on a victory in this war.

The German government has announced a national day of celebration in response to its victory, as victory parties erupt throughout the territory of the Reich. The American government has promised to continue fighting fascism wherever it can. The Russian government has promised that it will restore order to its territory and that this is not the end of their government.

options.name: All I have done has been for naught...
The German eagle swallows the Russian.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Wehrmacht Victorious
desc:
The Russian Republic has announced their unconditional surrender to the German Reich as the Russian army has failed in their goal to liberate Moscow. Already unrest has been reported in numerous Russian cities, with millions going to the streets demanding that President Zykov step down immediately. Local and national police units have been deployed to ensure that the protests remain peaceful.

Meanwhile in Germania, celebrations have already broken out, with a new decree from the Führer commemorating their victory over the Russians as a national holiday. Japan gave a muted response of dissatisfaction while America declared that democracy will never waver in the fight against Fascism. Elections are expected to be announced by President Zykov in order to calm the protestors.

options.name: The Slavs are defeated once more.
The Russians have lost yet another war.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Imperial Disaster
desc:
With the reunification of Russia under the Imperial banner, it seemed as though the tragedy of the early 20th century might finally have come to a close with the Tsardom emerging like a phoenix from the ashes. History however, has repeated once more. The Tsar Vladimir III has announced Russia’s capitulation to advancing German forces.

Already socialist, fascist and liberal elements have sprung up in fury to this news, and it seems likely Russia is headed towards another anarchy. The Tsar’s efforts to call for calm have failed as reports of riots and pandemonium sweep across Russia. Meanwhile, the Germans are in jubilation over their victory, as beer halls fill with Wehrmacht soldiers coming back from war. In Washington, the President has announced that no matter what, democracy will march on and that fascism will not prevail against liberty.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Broken Mercenaries
desc:
It seems as though history will never favor the Russian bear. Today, the United States of Russia has announced their total surrender to the German Reich, as the forces of Russia lost yet another battle against their sworn enemies. With the recent unification of Russia by Mitchell Werbell III, a notorious mercenary, it seemed as though Russia might finally have a chance to win against the Germans. However, this was not to be. Mass unrest has been reported following the announcement, alongside reports that Werbell has left the country amidst the chaos.

While Germania celebrates, Russia is leaderless. In America, they have been left frustrated as all their investment into Russia was for naught and democracy loses yet another ally. In a recent statement, the President of the United States declared that the American people will never bow to tyranny under any circumstance.

options.name: Who let foreigners rule our lands?

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Mathematician's Gamble Fails
desc:
Igor Shafarevich has announced the surrender of Russian forces to the German military following the failed invasion of the Reich's eastern territories. After the initial invasion, in which the Russians saw staggering success, much of the world hoped that this would finally be the war that would end Nazi tyranny over Europe. Yet, it seems that the Reich is to go on for many more years. Victory parties are being held in nearly every major city across Germany, while those in Russia turn back towards despair.

While Japan's reaction has been quite muted, the United States has promised that this is not the end of anti-fascism in Europe and that they will continue to fight to free the old world from oppression. Shafarevich, however, must contend with the consequences of his failed invasion as many question his continued competence in running the Russian nation as Russia weeps for her fallen.

options.name: Darkness reigns over the old world.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]German Reich Stands Victorious
desc:
The Russian National Soviet Republic has officially been defeated in its war against the German Reich. The RNSR, led by the self-proclaimed “New Marx” Ivan Serov, has been governed by a bizarre fusion of Soviet and Nazi ideology and has openly prioritized ethnic Russians in its policies. Serov claimed this fusion was the only way to save Russia in this third conflict with the Reich, but all his theories amounted to were thousands of dead Russians scattered across the Russian plains.

In the parts of Russia still not occupied by Germany, Russians tired of Serov’s oppressive rule and those humiliated by this defeat have taken up arms against Serov’s government. Meanwhile, Germany has won a resounding victory in the cold war, and proven its strength to the world. As celebrations erupt across the Reich's territories, it appears that a new era of prosperity may be dawning on Germany.

options.name: Who let foreigners rule our lands?
Russia cannot take much more of this.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Eurasian State Officially Surrenders
desc:
The Eurasian State has been defeated in its war against the German Reich. Eurasia, led by Lev Gumilyov’s Passionariyy, is a far-right state guided by the belief that Russians are ethnically and politically tied to the peoples of Asia. This claim has become reality, as most of Eurasia now permanently lies within the boundaries of Asia. In the parts of Russia still not occupied by Germany, those tired of Gumilyov’s neo-feudal rule have taken up arms against the Eurasian government. It remains to be seen if Gumilyov will survive the coming troubles.

With Germany's victory over the Eurasian state, it has further cemented its rule over the Old World. Celebrations have broken out from Rotterdam to colonial towns deep in the Russian plains.

options.name: The Eurasian dream is dead, and Russia with it.
The Untermensch have failed a final time.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Invasion Crumbles
desc:
It appears as if democracy has failed to triumph over fascism as Russian forces are mercilessly beaten back by the German Wehrmacht. The President of the Russian Republic has announced a conditional surrender to the Germans as celebrations erupt across major German cities. Throughout the free world the reaction has been subdued, with the American President calling the German victory “a dark day for global democracy.”

With this great victory for the German people, the political fractures of a few months prior have largely melted away into a new era of German pride and unity. In Russia, however, mass protests have erupted, demanding that their “weak and useless” leadership step down for new elections. With martial law being declared in many Russian cities, a new, dark era descends over the Russian people.

options.name: The Aryan has been proven superior!
The Russians are humbled once again...

title: [Get_newspaper_header]German Victory in the East
desc:
Darkness falls upon the old world once again as the forces of the Russian Republic begin a slow and painful retreat eastward following their surrender to the German Heer. Throughout the last days of the war, the government of the Republic faced mutinous army units alongside popular protests which paralyzed its governing capacity. It remains to be seen if the Republic can recover from this disaster.

The world’s response to this Russian defeat has been mixed. The German government rides a wave of patriotism and unity, with many citizens putting aside their differences to take a part in their country’s imposed greatness. The OFN is near catatonic, with secretive meetings and the redrawing of plans being all that the free world’s ambassadors will have to look forward to in the near future.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Bear Declawed
desc:
A massive defeat has been dealt to the Russian Federative Republic as its war against Nazi Germany ended in disaster when German forces overran the Russian army after months of fighting. Despite valiant efforts, the Russian troops were forced to retreat to the A-A line as the government began peace talks. In response to this, many Russians have started questioning the future of Russian democracy. Chaos and unrest have erupted across the country amid fears of a government collapse, with many citizens already fleeing the nation.

President Boris Yeltsin, who had been a symbol of hope and freedom for Russians during the war, fled for the United States shortly before the official surrender, leaving a leadership vacuum in the nation. With Russia collapsing and the Germans triumphant, freedom's torch has been extinguished in the old world.

options.name: The light of democracy has been extinguished in Russia.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Russian Liberation of Europe Fails
desc:
The world sits in silence as the Russian National Republic's once constant advance across the Einheitspakt's eastern territory has not only stalled, but been reversed entirely, with the Wehrmacht managing to beat back the Russian forces and force the signing of a treaty ending any Russian attempts to regain their lost territory.

As President Nikolay Petlin attempts to salvage any sense of stability in the wake of such a national tragedy, the OFN, who supported the National Republic in bolstering its war effort, expressed its condolences and hopes for the Russian people to fight on in their struggle against tyranny. Meanwhile, the Reich has celebrated its renewed dominance over Eastern Europe, with its Führer declaring triumph over "futile liberal aggression." As the Russian eagle falls, any semblance of hope for a free Europe appears to be lost to the march of the jackboot.

options.name: We have failed our people and the struggle for freedom.
We've beat them again, just as expected.
The Free World has failed once again.
The light of freedom in Europe is extinguished.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Imperial Reclamation Collapses
desc:
The worst has come to pass today as the Germans have declared victory over their Russian adversaries. While the White Army’s initial advances showed progress, the German Heer proved to be the better force as the Russians were slowly pushed back towards the A-A line, rolling back the Russian advance. Countless now flee the continent in a mass exodus not seen since Operation Barbarossa.

The loss has dealt a devastating blow to freedom in Europe, with the OFN stating that they will continue to fight for a Europe free of German tyranny. Meanwhile, Tsar Mikhail II urges his people to remain calm through this devastating loss as unrest continues to grow all across the Empire. Socialist agitation is spreading in the cities as some factions in the White Army question the Tsar’s leadership, with Russia hurtling towards another era of darkness.

options.name: The true Romanovs turn in their unmarked graves.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Rus’ Great Defeat
desc:
Today is a sad day for the Russian people as the government of Rus have announced a conditional surrender to the German army. Humiliated by this loss, Yuriy's legitimacy has been greatly weakened. Boris Krylov, heir to Rurik II, seems to some a viable replacement as a potential civil war looms over the defeated Russian nation.

In Germania celebrations abound as military parades, flanked by cheering onlookers, fill the crowded metropolis. Despite living in an era of increasing German political polarization, this victory has brought back levels of patriotism not seen for many years. The response elsewhere has been more muted, with the Japanese staying relatively silent while the Americans have reportedly sent ambassadors to give their condolences to those lost in the fight for Russian freedom.

options.name: This proves our will is superior!

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Rus Meet Defeat
desc:
The people of Russia have once more suffered defeat at the hands of superior German forces. Despite initial successes in which they seized much of the Russian plains and rolled back the forces of the Reichskommissariat Moskowien, the Heer managed to stem the tide and eventually turn them back, regaining their colonial territory with heavy losses on both sides. Faith in the Rurikid dynasty has been shaken as the reigning monarch of Russia, Ronegda I, finds herself as unpopular as the late Nicholas II.

Celebrations have erupted across the German Reich, many in costumes mocking the strange customs and fashions of the new Russia. The United States has promised that this is not the end of the fight against fascism. For Ronegda, however, her harsh policies towards the people with the promised goal of western liberation have turned to ash. Russia is now a powder keg waiting to explode.

options.name: We were promised glory, and found ashes.
Let them rot in their dark age.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The People’s Union's Advance Stalls
desc:
To the disappointment and fear of everyone in Russia and the Free World, the Russian People’s Union has lost in its bid to liberate Eastern Europe. Across the Union, many believed the invincible and legendary army would be able to defeat the beleaguered Wehrmacht, but this would not pass. After several months of brutal fighting, the army lost its cohesion and collapsed in on itself.

Celebrations are reported across Germany, with the Furher himself expected to appear in a televised speech. Meanwhile, Batov and his confidants are now trying to hold the Union together and recover from this loss. Several officials are attempting to find scapegoats for a loss which they believe to have been caused by dissidents as it seems the age of Russian instability has returned.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Reich Victorious over the Federation
desc:
The Russian flag lays in tatters for the fourth time this century as the overwhelming German counter-attack has forced Alexander Pokryshkin to negotiate a surrender with the German Reich. With mass evacuations from the frontlines taking place alongside general unrest following the announcement of the surrender, the Siloviks have begun to lose faith in the leadership of Pokryshkin.

In Germany, with victorious soldiers returning to their homes and families, a new era of peace and unity has begun as a feeling of mass patriotism swells across the war torn nation. In the OFN, war plans are being hastily redrawn as hushed political meetings are called to discuss what comes next. It appears that National Socialism's grip on Europe will continue for a long, long time...

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Whites Crumble Against the Reich
desc:
The forces of the White Army have finally met their match, with General Boris Shepunov declaring that the Russian Empire has surrendered to German forces as of eleven this morning. Despite early successes, the White Army was unable to hold on to their gains as the Germans pushed them back across the border. Now, the White Army returns home in tatters as the leadership finds itself in search of scapegoats to try and explain this disastrous defeat.

The people of the German Reich celebrate as the rest of the world mourns what could have been the dismantling of the Nazi empire. Back in Russia, Boris Shepunov and the Tsar are in heated discussions as to what happens next. The White's grip on their empire is slipping as chants not heard since 1917 are heard across major Russian cities. Russia appears to be headed towards many more years of chaos and despair.

options.name: The German eagle flies higher than ever!
Not even an empire could save Russia.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]German Triumph in Russia
desc:
Momentous days fall upon the world as the Second West Russian War ends in much the same way as the first, with a German Victory. Sergei Bunyachenko, ruler of the Russian state, has reportedly disappeared from the public eye as the situation on the streets deteriorates into near-anarchy. Having come from a group that betrayed the Red Army during the first West Russian War, the streets are filled with the whispers that Sergei may have intended for Russia to lose once more

In Germania, a more positive atmosphere fills the streets, as mass celebrations have erupted in many urban centers. Political divisions have melted away, and a new united German people have arisen from the troubles of the 70s. Slowly but surely, the entire world has begun to realize that the German Reich will be around for a long, long time.

options.name: The traitor's redemption crumbles to ashes.
The Aryan is supreme once again!

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Fascist Revolution Collapses
desc:
Russia seems condemned to defeat for the rest of time. Four times in the last century has she been mutilated under governments of all colors. Today in Riga, the Germans and Russians have agreed on a settlement for peace, officially ending the Russian War of National Reclamation in an unforgettable defeat from the country of her own inspiration. What many are terming a civil war of the fascist world has proven German dominance supreme once more.

This all comes after increasingly desperate attempts by the Amur administration to win the war served as a spark for the spreading a fire of national discontent, strikes, and international condemnation. The streets of almost every Russian city are crowded with dissidents, with no foreseeable end to the war against the Russian people. The Russian tragedy marches on as the German eagle soars higher than ever.

options.name: Next time, we shall burn Berlin.
The tears of the East fall mute.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Spicket Runs Dry
desc:
In one of the strangest turn of events this century, the Reich has triumphed over a Russia ruled by German capital.
